trust.title: How Adera works
trust.intro: Adera is built so that reviews can be trusted — by readers, reviewers, and businesses alike. This page explains the rules every review and rating follows.

sections.title: The rating you see is never adjusted
paragraphs: The average shown for a place is the plain average of its published reviews, rounded to two decimals. We never boost or lower it.
The full star distribution is always shown, so you can see how many people gave one star and how many gave five.

Rankings such as “top rated” use a separate, public formula that pulls places with few reviews toward a neutral 3.5, so one five-star review can’t beat a hundred good ones. That score is never shown as the rating.

sections.title: Small numbers are labeled as small
paragraphs: Percentages such as “would recommend” are only shown once at least 5 people have answered. Below that, we show the counts instead.
Every rating carries a confidence level based on how many reviews it rests on: very few (under 3), low (under 10), medium (under 30), or high.

sections.title: What “verified” means
paragraphs: A review is only labeled verified after a moderator has checked private proof — a receipt, an order screenshot, or a location code. A photo on its own adds context but does not make a review verified.
Proof is stored privately, is visible only to the reviewer and our moderators, and is never shown publicly.

sections.title: Paid or connected reviews are labeled
paragraphs: Reviewers are asked whether they received anything for their review or have a connection to the business. Any answer other than “no” appears as a label on the review — the review stays, and readers can judge for themselves.

sections.title: Businesses can respond, not remove
paragraphs: A business can post one public response to each review and can report a review it believes breaks the rules. There is no way — paid or otherwise — for a business to delete, change, or hide a customer’s review.

sections.title: How moderation works
paragraphs: Reviews are published straight away. Reports never hide a review automatically; only a moderator’s decision can, and every decision is recorded.

You can report a review for spam, a made-up experience, a hidden conflict of interest, harassment, hate speech, sharing personal information, an unsupported accusation, being off-topic, being a duplicate, or manipulated evidence.

sections.title: Limits that keep reviews fair
paragraphs: Each person can review a place once every 30 days — after that they update their existing review — and can post at most 5 reviews a day.

sections.title: Reality Check
paragraphs: For restaurants and cafés, people who found a place on social media are asked whether it matched what they saw online. We show the combined answers — never accusations against a particular creator — and only as percentages once at least 5 people have answered.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: What Adera collects about you, why, who else sees it, how long it is kept, and how to get a copy or have it erased. It describes what the service actually does today.
privacy.contact: Questions or requests about your data: {{email}}.
privacy.contactInApp: To see or erase your data, use Account in the app: “Download my data” and “Delete account”.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: Your account: the display name you choose, your email address or phone number, and your password, which is stored only as a one-way hash.
What you write: reviews, ratings, the optional details you add (such as the date of your visit, the price you paid, or a link to your post about it), the places you add, reports, and votes.
Photos you attach to a review. Before a photo is published we re-encode it, which removes its hidden metadata, including the location it was taken.
Receipts and other proof you submit to verify a review. These are private: only you and our moderators can open them, through links that expire after minutes.

To keep reviews honest: for each review, a scrambled code made from the network you were on (the first part of your internet address, never the full address) and a random identifier for your copy of the app. They are kept 90 days and seen only by moderators, to spot many reviews coming from one place.
For signing in and notifications: which device and app version each sign-in came from, and your device's notification token if you allow notifications.
If you use “Near me”, your approximate location is sent to find nearby places. It is used for that search only and is not stored.

sections.title: Why we use it
paragraphs: To run your account and show your reviews; to keep the platform free of fake and abusive reviews; to send you the notifications you asked for, such as a business replying to your review; and to keep the service secure.
We do not sell your data, show advertising, or use analytics or tracking services.

sections.title: What is public
paragraphs: Your display name, your reviews and their details, your photos, and how many reviews you have written are public, on the web and in the app.
Your email, phone number, account ID, receipts, and the codes kept to prevent fraud are never public.

sections.title: Who else handles it
paragraphs: We use a small number of service providers to run Adera: our hosting and database providers (Render and Neon, with servers in Frankfurt, Germany), an email service to send sign-in and verification codes, and Google Firebase to deliver notifications to Android phones. They process data only to provide those services to us.
This means your data is stored and processed outside Ethiopia, in the European Union.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Your account data is kept while you have an account. Fraud-prevention codes are deleted after 90 days.
Deactivating your account hides nothing and deletes nothing; signing in again reactivates it.
Deleting your account (erasure) is described below.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: See your data: “Download my data” in the app gives you everything we hold about you in a file, including links to your photos and receipts.
Correct it: you can change your name and edit or remove your reviews at any time.

Erase it: “Delete account” in the app signs you out everywhere at once and erases your account seven days later. Signing in during those seven days cancels it. Erasure deletes your name, email, phone, password, photos, receipts, notifications and fraud-prevention codes. Your reviews and ratings stay, shown as by a “Former member”, because they describe real experiences other people rely on, and deleting them on request would let a business pressure reviewers into removing criticism. If you want a review gone too, remove it before deleting your account.
You can also object to how we use your data, or complain to Ethiopia's data protection authority.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Connections to Adera are encrypted, passwords and codes are stored only as hashes, and receipts are kept in private storage. If a breach puts your data at risk, we will tell you and the authority as the law requires.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If we change this notice, we will update the date above, and tell you in the app if the change matters to how your data is used.
